# Elpod

> Elpod is an early-stage, decorator-free application framework for modular Elysia services on Bun. It adds explicit constructor dependency injection, feature pods, provider lifetimes, lifecycle management, and architecture checks while preserving native Elysia routes.

- Canonical website: https://elpod.vercel.app/
- Documentation: https://elpod.vercel.app/docs/
- GitHub organization: https://github.com/elpodjs
- Source: https://github.com/elpodjs/core
- Documentation source: https://github.com/elpodjs/docs
- Packages: `@elpod/core`, `@elpod/cli`, `create-elpod`
- Runtime: Bun 1.4+ with Elysia; TypeScript and ESM
- License: MIT
- Status: working alpha; pin versions and review changes before upgrading

## Start

```sh
bun create elpod my-app
cd my-app
bun run dev
```

Elpod uses native Elysia `routes(app)` methods in controllers. Classes declare constructor dependencies with `static readonly inject = [Service] as const` or `needs`. A `pod({...})` groups a controller, URL prefix, providers, and explicit dependency boundaries. `application({ features: [pod] })` assembles the application. Request-scoped providers are resolved through `injectHandler()`; `ElpodContract<typeof app>` exposes pod route types to Eden Treaty.

```ts
import { application, pod, type ElpodElysia } from "@elpod/core";

class OrdersService { list() { return [{ id: "order-1" }]; } }
class OrdersController {
  static readonly inject = [OrdersService] as const;
  constructor(private readonly orders: OrdersService) {}
  routes(app: ElpodElysia) { return app.get("/", () => this.orders.list()); }
}
const orders = pod({ name: "orders", prefix: "/orders", controller: OrdersController, providers: [OrdersService] });
export const app = application({ features: [orders] });
```

- [Elpod vs NestJS](https://elpod.vercel.app/docs/compare/elpod-vs-nestjs/)

Elpod is an application-structure layer, not an Elysia replacement, ORM, identity provider, durable broker, or deployment platform. Adapters and operational guarantees remain application-owned. This file is a convenience index for agents; the HTML documentation is the canonical reference.
